LESSON: HEAT

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
Strand: Force and Energy
Topic 3.3: Heat

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Heat. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What are the safety measures observed when using heat?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify sources of heat in nature
2. demonstrate uses of heat in day-to-day life
3. describe safety measures to observe when using heat

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: HEAT
Subject: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Heat helps you succeed in SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: HEAT
Heat is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Identify sources of heat in nature

What this means
In this part you learn to identify sources of heat in nature. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify sources of heat in nature.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Heat” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify sources of heat in nature. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Demonstrate uses of heat in day-to-day life

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate uses of heat in day-to-day life. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate uses of heat in day-to-day life.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Heat matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate uses of heat in day-to-day life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe safety measures to observe when using heat

What this means
In this part you learn to describe safety measures to observe when using heat. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe safety measures to observe when using heat.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Heat this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe safety measures to observe when using heat. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Heat is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Heat” around your school. (skill: identify sources of heat in nature)

Example 2: Say why Heat matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: demonstrate uses of heat in day-to-day life)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Heat this week. (skill: describe safety measures to observe when using heat)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Heat to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify sources of heat in nature.
3. Practise this skill: demonstrate uses of heat in day-to-day life.
4. Practise this skill: describe safety measures to observe when using heat.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Heat from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Heat: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Heat?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are the safety measures observed when using heat?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Heat means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify sources of heat in nature.
5. Be able to: demonstrate uses of heat in day-to-day life.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
